merger_description:
Loftware Inc. (**Loftware**) proposes to acquire Sigma Guarantor LLC (**Seagull Parent**) and its subsidiaries (together, **Seagull**), via a series of intermediary transactions set out in the Purchase Agreement (the **Acquisition**).

As part of the Acquisition, investment funds managed by Accel KKR (**AKKR**) and Riverside Healthcare Partners (**Riverside**) will contribute equity to fund the Acquisition, in exchange for further interests in a Loftware parent entity. Loftware is majority owned and jointly controlled by AKKR and Riverside Funds, and will continue to be post-acquisition.

Seagull is majority-owned and controlled by funds managed by Peak Rock Capital (**Peak Rock**).

Seagull develops and supplies software used to design, manage and automate labels, barcodes, Radio-Frequency Identification tags and related types of identification (labelling software) and tracking processes (track and trace software). Seagull's principal product is its BarTender platform. Its labelling software is primarily provided as an 'on-premises solution', supplied indirectly via distributors and is targeted at businesses with less complex requirements.

Loftware also develops and supplies labelling software but does not supply track and trace services, including in Australia. Loftware's labelling software is primarily supplied as a cloud-based solution, which is targeted at larger companies with more complex requirements.

AKKR is a technology-focused private equity investor with investments in a range of software and technology businesses. Through its portfolio companies, AKKR has interests in a range of differentiated businesses that supply software to business customers across a variety of industries.

Riverside is a private equity investor that focuses on investments in founder-owned healthcare companies in the lower middle market.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition, given:
a. there is a small horizontal overlap between Loftware and
Seagull Software in the supply of labelling software services
and the increase in share of supply arising from the
Acquisition would be small
b. there are numerous alternative suppliers of labelling
software services to customers in Australia
c. there is a low risk of foreclosure or other concerning vertical
effects resulting from exclusionary conduct post-acquisition.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
